newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bomb blast rocks city in northern Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast rocks city in northern Colombia.

text.p: A bomb planted by suspected leftist guerrillas rocked the capital of Colombia's northern province of Cesar early Thursday, causing extensive damage but no deaths or serious injuries, authorities said.

Police said the bomb -- about 44 pounds (20 kg) of dynamite -- exploded shortly after midnight, shattering the windows of at least 11 shops, banks and residences in the downtown area of the city near Colombia's northernmost border with Venezuela.
It was detonated near the home of former Sen. Jose Guillermo Castro, who suffered minor injuries in the explosion along with three night-watchmen, police spokesmen said.
Castro, a leader of the ruling Liberal Party, could not be reached immediately for comment. Radio reports said he had been the target of at least one assassination attempt by leftist guerrillas.

A ranch belonging to Castro was the target of a recent bomb attack by Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels. Police sources said they suspected Thursday's bombing was also the work of FARC rebels.
